compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Prior written permission to erect/install a new lift, escalator or moving walk from the Electrical Inspector (Lifts)/Chief Electrical Inspector before starting erection and the same must be carried out only through an approved (licensed) contractor.
action_required:
Obtain Prior Approval: Apply for and receive written permission from the Electrical Inspector (Lifts)/Chief Electrical Inspector before starting installation of any new lift, escalator, or moving walk.
Do Not Start Erection Without Approval: Ensure no installation or erection work begins until the required permission is granted.
Use an Approved Contractor: Engage only a licensed/approved lift contractor for erection and installation activities.
Maintain Documentation: Keep copies of approvals, contractor licenses, and installation records for compliance verification.
forms_documents:
Copies of approvals, 
Contractor licenses, 
Installation records
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33). Erection without permission is also a direct contravention of Section 4(4).
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Give written notice of completion to the Electrical Inspector (Lifts) and apply for a licence to work/use it within one month of completing erection
action_required:
Submit Completion Notice: Within one month of completing the erection of the lift, escalator, or moving walk, provide a written notice of completion to the Electrical Inspector (Lifts).
Apply for Operating Licence: Along with or after the completion notice, apply for the required licence to work/use the lift, escalator, or moving walk.
Maintain Supporting Documents: Keep installation completion records, inspection reports, test certificates, and licence application documents for regulatory review.
Do Not Operate Without Licence: Ensure the lift, escalator, or moving walk is not put into use until the required licence is obtained from the competent authority.
Confirm that the completion notice was submitted within one month of installation and that an application for the licence to operate/use has been filed with the Electrical Inspector (Lifts).
forms_documents:
Installation completion records, inspection reports, 
test certificates, and licence application documents
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33). Using the lift/escalator/moving walk without a working licence is a separate contravention of Section 11.
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Licence to be renewed after the expiry of 20 years validity which may be granted for 5 years.
action_required:
Track Licence Validity: Maintain records of the working licence and monitor its 20-year validity period from the date of grant.
Apply for Renewal Before Expiry: Submit a renewal application to the Electrical Inspector (Lifts) well before the licence expiration date.
Maintain Documentation: Keep copies of the licence, renewal applications, inspection reports, maintenance records, and modernization certificates.

Verify that the operating licence is valid, renewal applications are submitted before expiry, maintenance requirements are met, and any safety upgrades required by the Electrical Inspector have been completed.
forms_documents: Copies of the licence, renewal applications, inspection reports, maintenance records, and modernization certificates.
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33). Failure to renew in time means the installation cannot lawfully continue to be worked/used (Section 11); Electrical Inspector (Lifts) may also refuse renewal or order use to be discontinued.
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Prior written permission of the Electrical Inspector in case of  addition or alteration that changes in characteristics of a lift/escalator/moving walk  except changes directed underunsafe condition orders).
action_required:
Obtain Prior Approval for Modifications: Secure written permission from the Electrical Inspector (Lifts) before making any addition or alteration that changes the characteristics of a lift, escalator, or moving walk.
Assess Impact of Changes: Review proposed modifications to determine whether they affect parameters such as:
Passenger/load capacity
Speed
Number of stops/floors
Number of steps or other operational characteristics
Submit Required Documentation: Provide technical details, drawings, and specifications of the proposed changes as required by the authority.
Maintain Approval Records: Retain copies of permissions, modification records, and updated technical documents for inspection and audit purposes.
Exception: Prior permission is not required where changes are carried out pursuant to directions issued under Section 21 relating to unsafe conditions.

Confirm that any modification affecting the operational characteristics of the lift, escalator, or moving walk has received prior written approval from the Electrical Inspector (Lifts).
forms_documents: Copies of permissions, modification records, and updated technical documents for inspection and audit purposes.
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33).
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Save where the Act/Rules provide otherwise, the relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Code of Practice must be followed; specifications of the lift/escalator/moving walk and the materials/apparatus used in it must conform to the relevant BIS specifications (or the prescribed rules, where BIS specifications do not exist).
action_required:
Adhere to Applicable BIS Standards: Ensure the design, installation, operation, maintenance, and testing of lifts, escalators, and moving walks comply with the relevant Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) Codes of Practice.
Use BIS-Compliant Equipment and Materials: Verify that all materials, components, apparatus, and equipment used conform to the applicable BIS specifications.
Follow Prescribed Rules Where BIS Standards Are Not Available: In cases where no relevant BIS specification exists, comply with the requirements prescribed under the Act and Rules.
Obtain and Maintain Compliance Documentation: Keep records of technical specifications, manufacturer certificates, conformity certificates, and test reports demonstrating compliance with applicable standards.
Conduct Periodic Review: Regularly review installations and maintenance practices to ensure continued adherence to updated BIS standards and regulatory requirements.

Confirm that the lift, escalator, or moving walk design, equipment, materials, installation, and maintenance conform to applicable BIS Codes/Specifications or prescribed statutory requirements where BIS standards are unavailable.
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33). Non-conforming installations can also be refused erection permission/working licence, or later be declared unsafe under Section 21.
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Maintenance contract with an approved (licensed) contractor for satisfactory maintenance of the lift/escalator/moving walk, covering cleaning, oiling, adjusting and repairing till the handover to the Society
action_required:
Enter into a Maintenance Contract: Ensure a valid maintenance contract is executed with an approved/licensed contractor for each lift, escalator, or moving walk.
Engage Only Licensed Contractors: Verify that the maintenance contractor holds a valid licence/approval under the Act.
Cover Essential Maintenance Activities: The maintenance contract should include:
Cleaning
Oiling/Lubrication
Adjustments
Repairs
Routine preventive maintenance
Maintain Maintenance Records: Keep copies of the maintenance agreement, service reports, inspection records, and repair logs for regulatory inspection.
Monitor Contractor Performance: Ensure periodic maintenance is carried out as per the contract to maintain safe and satisfactory operation.

Confirm that a current maintenance contract is in place with a licensed contractor and that regular maintenance activities are being performed and documented.
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33). Proper maintenance is also a pre-condition for renewal of the working licence under Section 8(3).
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Third-party insurance is in place to cover the risk to passengers using it till the handover to the society
action_required:
Obtain Third-Party Insurance: Ensure that a valid third-party insurance policy is in place for every lift, escalator, or moving walk after completion of erection.
Cover Passenger Risks: The insurance should adequately cover liabilities and risks arising to passengers using the lift, escalator, or moving walk.
Maintain Continuous Coverage: Monitor policy validity and renew the insurance policy before expiry to avoid any lapse in coverage.
Maintain Insurance Records: Keep copies of insurance policies, renewal certificates, and related documents readily available for inspection and compliance purposes.
Review Coverage Periodically: Ensure the insured amount and policy terms remain adequate based on usage, capacity, and statutory requirements.

Confirm that a valid third-party insurance policy covering passenger risks has been obtained and remains active for each lift, escalator, or moving walk.
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33).
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Maharashtra Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks Act, 2017
brief_description: Maintenance of  a log book for each lift, escalator or moving walk, recording details of its operation, breakdowns (other than failure of electrical supply) and any accidents for the inspection of Electrical Inspector.
action_required:
Maintain a Log Book: Keep a separate log book for each lift, escalator, and moving walk.
Record Key Events: Ensure the log book captures:
Operational details
Breakdowns or malfunctions (excluding electrical power supply failures)
Accidents and incidents
Repairs and corrective actions taken

Update Records Regularly: Enter details promptly and accurately whenever an event occurs.
Retain Records for Inspection: Keep log books readily available for review by the Electrical Inspector (Lifts).
Ensure Accessibility and Accuracy: Maintain complete and up-to-date records to demonstrate safe operation and regulatory compliance.

Verify that a log book is maintained for each lift, escalator, and moving walk, containing records of operation, breakdowns, and accidents, and that it is available for inspection by the Electrical Inspector (Lifts).
penalty: Fine up to Rs. 50,000; and for a continuing contravention, an additional fine up to Rs. 1,000 for every day of continued default after conviction (Section 32). Officers in charge of a firm/company can also be held liable (Section 33).
applicability: Applicable only where the building has a lift, escalator or moving walk

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Compliance with prescribed fire protection and life safety requirements, including installation, maintenance, and operational readiness of emergency response systems and evacuation arrangements.
action_required:
Comply with Fire & Life Safety Requirements: Ensure the building meets all applicable fire protection and life safety provisions prescribed under the National Building Code (NBC).
Install Required Fire Safety Systems: Provide appropriate fire detection, alarm, suppression, firefighting, and emergency communication systems as required for the building occupancy and risk category.
Maintain Fire Protection Systems: Conduct regular inspection, testing, and maintenance of fire safety equipment and systems to ensure operational effectiveness.
Ensure Operational Readiness: Keep all emergency response systems, firefighting equipment, exits, and evacuation routes functional, accessible, and free from obstruction at all times.
Establish Evacuation Arrangements: Maintain emergency evacuation plans, signage, assembly points, and emergency procedures, and conduct periodic drills where applicable.
Maintain Compliance Records: Retain inspection reports, maintenance logs, testing certificates, fire drill records, and statutory approvals for audit and regulatory inspections.

Verify that required fire protection and life safety systems are installed, regularly maintained, operationally ready, and supported by documented emergency response and evacuation procedures in accordance with the National Building Code
forms_documents: Inspection reports, maintenance logs, testing certificates, fire drill records, and statutory approvals for audit and regulatory inspections.
penalty: Rejection of building occupancy, structural sealing, or penal fines linked with local municipal bylaws.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Operated and maintained in a safe condition through regular inspections, testing, certification, and preventive maintenance activities.
action_required:
Conduct Regular Inspections: Periodically inspect all electrical installations and equipment.
Perform Testing and Certification: Ensure electrical systems are tested and certified as required.
Implement Preventive Maintenance: Carry out scheduled maintenance to prevent electrical hazards and failures.

Verify that electrical installations are regularly inspected, tested, certified, and maintained in a safe operating condition.
penalty: Under Section 146 of the Electricity Act, a fine up to ₹100,000 for companies, and daily fines up to ₹5,000 for persistent defaults.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Segregate waste produced at source and processed, stored, and disposed of in accordance with the provisions of the Solid Waste Management Rules.
action_required:
Segregate Waste at Source: Separate biodegradable, recyclable, and other waste streams at the point of generation.
Ensure Proper Storage: Store waste in designated containers and locations.
Use Authorized Disposal Methods: Dispose of waste through approved collection and processing agencies.
Maintain Records: Keep waste disposal and vendor documentation.

Verify that waste is segregated, stored, and disposed of in accordance with the Solid Waste Management Rules.
penalty: Spot fines from ₹500 up to ₹25,000 per violation based on municipal limits under NGT "Polluter Pays" frameworks.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Store, handle, and dispose off  only through authorized recyclers or dismantlers as prescribed under the Rules.
action_required:
Segregate E-Waste: Identify and separately store electronic and electrical waste.
Use Authorized Recyclers: Dispose of e-waste only through authorized recyclers or dismantlers.
Maintain Disposal Records: Retain handover acknowledgements and certificates from recyclers.
Prevent Unauthorized Disposal: Ensure e-waste is not mixed with general waste.

Verify that all e-waste is disposed of through authorized recyclers and supporting records are maintained.
forms_documents: Handover acknowledgements and certificates from recyclers
penalty: Environmental Compensation (EC) charges calculated by CPCB based on volume, or up to 5 years imprisonment / ₹1 Lakh fine under Section 15 of EPA.

regulation: Factories Act, 1948 / State Shops & Establishments Act
brief_description: Ensure hygienic working conditions with regular cleaning and maintenance
action_required:
Maintain Workplace Cleanliness: Keep premises clean, sanitary, and free from waste accumulation.
Ensure Hygiene Standards: Conduct regular cleaning and sanitation activities.
Control Health Hazards: Implement pest control and housekeeping measures.
Monitor Workplace Conditions: Periodically inspect work areas for cleanliness and safety.

Verify that the workplace is maintained in a clean, hygienic, and safe condition.
penalty: General penalty under Section 92: Fine up to ₹3,000,000 for corporate office offenses; repeating an offense risks up to 2 years imprisonment.

brief_description: Use vehicles having valid insurance only
action_required:
Obtain Vehicle Insurance: Ensure all company vehicles have valid insurance coverage.
Track Policy Expiry Dates: Monitor insurance validity and renew before expiry.
Maintain Insurance Records: Keep copies of policies and renewal documents.
Prevent Uninsured Vehicle Use: Do not operate vehicles without insurance.

Verify that all company-operated vehicles have valid insurance coverage
forms_documents: Copies of policies and renewal documents
penalty: Punishable under Section 196: ₹2,000 fine and/or up to 3 months imprisonment for the 1st offense.
applicability: Applicable only where the company owns/operates motor vehicles

brief_description: Valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) Certificate is to be maintained
action_required:
Obtain PUC Certificates: Ensure vehicles undergo emission checks as required.
Renew PUC Timely: Monitor and renew certificates before expiry.
Maintain Records: Keep valid PUC certificates for all applicable vehicles.
Monitor Emission Compliance: Rectify vehicles failing emission standards.

Verify that all applicable vehicles possess valid PUC certificates.
penalty: Punishable under Section 190(2): ₹10,000 fine plus driving license disqualification for 3 months for a single lapse.
applicability: Applicable only where the company owns/operates motor vehicles

brief_description: No person shall drive a motor vehicle unless they hold an effective and valid driving licence authorizing them to drive that category of vehicle.
action_required:
Verify Driving Licences: Check validity of drivers' licences before vehicle assignment.
Ensure Licence Suitability: Confirm licences are appropriate for the vehicle category.
Maintain Licence Records: Retain copies of valid driving licences.
Monitor Renewals: Track licence expiry dates and renewals.

Verify that all drivers possess valid and appropriate driving licences.
penalty: Punishable under Section 181: Fine of ₹5,000 levied against the driver.
applicability: Applicable only where the company owns/operates motor vehicles

brief_description: valid passports and maintain updated passport-related records to be maintened fro employees undertaking international travel on official assignments.
action_required:
Verify Passport Validity: Ensure employees travelling internationally hold valid passports.
Track Expiry Dates: Monitor passport validity before overseas travel.
Maintain Passport Records: Keep updated passport details for travelling employees.
Ensure Timely Renewals: Complete passport renewals before expiry where required.

Verify that employees undertaking international travel possess valid passports and updated records are maintained.
penalty: Fine up to ₹5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years for providing false deployment declarations or unverified credentials.
applicability: Applicable only when employees undertake official international travel

regulation: Maharashtra Fire Prevention & Life Safety Measures Act, 2023
brief_description: Prescribed fire-prevention and life-safety measures and maintain them in good repair/efficient condition
action_required: Identify building classification; provide all prescribed active/passive fire systems; maintain them continuously and renew the annual Fire NOC/safety certification with the local fire authority.
forms_documents:
1. Sanction Plans- 1 Sets
2. Evaluation checklist
3. Architect Application
4. Provisional Fire NOC
5. Commencement certificate.
6. Electrical contractor certificate
7. Lift Licence.
8. Undertaking
9. Authorization letter
10. DG set purchase order

brief_description: Registration of every establishment employing building workers.
action_required:
Register the establishment with the registering officer under the BOCW Act before commencing building/construction work employing building workers.

Submit Form XII in triplicate to the Registering Officer within 60 days of starting work if you employ 10+ workers. Attach building plan, land documents, and challan.

reference_section: Section 38(2) of the BOCW Act and Rule 209 of the BOCW Central Rules, 1998
brief_description: Safety Officer to be appointed in establishments employing 500 or more workers.
action_required: Appoint a qualified Safety Officer at any site/establishment employing 500 or more building workers and notify the appointment to the authority.
applicability: Applicable only where 500 or more building workers are employed at the establishment

reference_section: Section 38(1) of the BOCW Act and Rule 208 of the BOCW Central Rules, 1998
brief_description: Constitute and function the Safety Committee.
action_required: Constitute a Safety Committee with worker and management representation and hold its meetings/functions monthly, maintaining minutes.
due_date: Non-compliance may attract action by Labour Authority.

brief_description: Prescribe safety and health measures; many State BOCW Rules specifically require a Health & Safety Policy for large projects.
action_required: Adopt and implement a documented Health & Safety Policy covering the safety and health measures prescribed for the project.
due_date: May be treated as safety management deficiency.

brief_description: Provide information, instruction, training and supervision to workers regarding safety.
action_required: Conduct monthly safety information, instruction, training and supervision sessions for workers and maintain attendance/training records.
penalty: May lead to enforcement action after accidents.

brief_description: Safety requirements for ladders, roofs, working platforms, guardrails, fall protection and work at height.
action_required: Provide and inspect ladders, roofs, working platforms, guardrails and fall-protection systems monthly to ensure compliance with height-work safety rules.

brief_description: Design, erection, inspection and safe use of scaffolds by competent persons.
action_required: Ensure scaffolds are designed, erected and inspected monthly by a competent person before use, with records maintained.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Excavation, trenching, shoring, sloping, barricading and safe access.
action_required: Implement and monthly inspect excavation/trenching safeguards - shoring, sloping, barricading and safe access - at all active excavation sites.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: First aid boxes, trained first aid personnel and medical facilities.
action_required: Provide adequately stocked first-aid boxes, trained first-aid personnel and on-site medical facilities as prescribed, and verify one-time compliance at project start.
penalty: Penalty for non-compliance.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Establish procedures for emergencies such as fire, collapse and rescue.
action_required: Establish and document an Emergency Response Plan covering fire, collapse and rescue procedures, and review/update it monthly.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Periodic emergency drills are generally mandated through State BOCW Rules
action_required: Conduct periodic (monthly) emergency mock drills as per the project safety plan and maintain drill records.
penalty: Inspection observations.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Employers shall provide and ensure use of suitable PPE including helmets, safety belts, shoes, gloves, eye and respiratory protection.
action_required: Issue suitable PPE (helmets, safety belts, shoes, gloves, eye/respiratory protection) to all workers and monitor usage monthly.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Examination, testing, certification and safe use of cranes, hoists, lifting tackles and lifting appliances by competent persons.
action_required: Get cranes, hoists, lifting tackles and lifting appliances examined, tested and certified by a competent person on a monthly basis and maintain certificates.
applicability: Applicable only where cranes, hoists or lifting appliances are deployed at site

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Installation, testing, examination, certification and commissioning before use.
action_required: Obtain installation testing, examination, certification and commissioning clearance for lifting equipment before it is first put into use.
forms_documents: TPI Certificate, Load Test Certificate, Erection & Commissioning Certificate (maintained on site)
due_date: Before first use, after re-erection, alteration or major repair
penalty: Equipment may be prohibited from operation, legal action and liability in case of accidents.
applicability: Applicable only where cranes, hoists or lifting appliances are deployed at site

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Periodic inspection, maintenance and safe operation of machinery and lifting equipment.
action_required: Draw up and follow a periodic inspection and maintenance schedule for machinery and lifting equipment to ensure safe operation.
forms_documents: Preventive Maintenance Records, Equipment Inspection Register
due_date: As per manufacturer's schedule and project requirements
penalty: Penalties for unsafe machinery; increased liability in case of incidents.
applicability: Applicable only where cranes, hoists or lifting appliances are deployed at site

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Machinery and lifting equipment shall be operated only by trained and competent persons.
action_required: Permit machinery and lifting equipment to be operated only by trained and certified/competent operators; maintain competency records.
due_date: Before deployment of operator and whenever a new operator is assigned
penalty: Legal liability and penalties for operation by unqualified personnel.
applicability: Applicable only where cranes, hoists or lifting appliances are deployed at site

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Safe Working Load (SWL), load charts, lifting accessories and lifting operations shall comply with statutory requirements.
action_required: Display Safe Working Load (SWL) and load charts on lifting equipment and ensure lifting operations/accessories comply with statutory limits.
forms_documents: Lifting Accessories Test Certificates, SWL Certificates
due_date: Before use and at prescribed intervals
penalty: Unsafe lifting operations may lead to prohibition of use, penalties and accident liability.
applicability: Applicable only where cranes, hoists or lifting appliances are deployed at site

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (as implemented) and BOCW Act
reference_section: Sections 38–41 of the BOCW Act and Section 6 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
brief_description: Ensure safe plant, machinery, systems of work, supervision and welfare of workers.
action_required: Ensure plant, machinery, systems of work, supervision and worker welfare facilities meet the safety standards under the BOCW Act and OSH Code, and review annually.
forms_documents: SOPs, Pre-start Checklists, Incident Reports (where applicable)
due_date: Continuous throughout project duration and immediately upon any unsafe condition
penalty: Regulatory action, work stoppage, fines and prosecution in case of serious violations or accidents.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: The ambient air quality standards in respect of noise for different areas/zones shall be such as specified in the Schedule.
action_required: Monitor and keep ambient noise levels within the zone-wise standards specified in the Schedule on an ongoing basis.
penalty: Action under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986; closure directions, environmental compensation and prosecution.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: The State Government shall categorize areas into industrial, commercial, residential or silence areas/zones.
action_required: Confirm the project site's area classification (industrial/commercial/residential/silence zone) as notified by the State Government and plan activities accordingly.
penalty: Regulatory action for non-compliance with applicable standards.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: A loudspeaker or public address system shall not be used except after obtaining written permission from the authority.
action_required: Obtain written permission from the competent authority before using any loudspeaker or public address system at the site.
forms_documents: FSI Calculation Sheet verified by Architect
penalty: Seizure, stoppage of event, prosecution and local authority action.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Sound emitting construction equipment shall not be used during night time in residential areas and silence zones except in public interest.
action_required: Schedule construction equipment operation to avoid night-time use in residential areas and silence zones, except where permitted in public interest.
forms_documents: Water Connection Application submitted to Municipal Water Dept
penalty: Work stoppage, environmental compensation and prosecution.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Construction activities shall be undertaken in compliance with prescribed noise restrictions and timing requirements.
action_required: Schedule construction activities to comply with prescribed noise restrictions and permitted working hours.
penalty: Stop-work directions and environmental penalties.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)

brief_description: Environment clerance is to be obtained for those project whose BUA area is 20000 Sqm and and above or area covering 50ha are applicable to get Environment clerance
action_required: For projects with built-up area of 20,000 sq.m and above (or covering 50 ha+), apply for and obtain Environment Clearance (EC) from SEIAA/MoEFCC before commencement; track the 10-year validity and apply for revision/amendment for any project change.

action_required: Within 7 days of the date of issue of the EC, in at least two widely circulated local newspapers, one in the vernacular language.
penalty: None

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Environment clearance Act 2006 and its subsequent amendment
brief_description: consent to Establish , should be taken before initiation of construction activity on site
action_required: Apply for and obtain Consent to Establish (CTE) from the State Pollution Control Board before initiating any construction activity on site; renew every 5 years or as specified.
penalty: non receipt /revalidation after valid period, as well as non submission of BG as per the condition stipulated CTE

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Environment clearance Act 2006 and its subsequent amendment

action_required: Obtain Consent to Operate (CTO) from the State Pollution Control Board before/at the time of Occupation Certificate, and renew within the specified 1-5 year validity.
penalty: non receipt /revalidation after valid period, as well as non submission of BG as per the condition stipulated CTO

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Environment clearance Act 2006 and its subsequent amendment
brief_description: Environment statement ,should be submmited on every finanacial year
action_required: Prepare and submit the Environmental Statement (Form V) to the State Pollution Control Board by the prescribed date every financial year.
penalty: None

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
reference_section: As per CGWA act as well as EC condition
brief_description: Obtain NOC from CGWA auhtority in case of  extraction of ground water
action_required: Where groundwater is extracted, apply for and obtain a No Objection Certificate from the Central Ground Water Authority before commencing/continuing extraction.
penalty: Yes
applicability: Applicable only where the project extracts groundwater

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
brief_description: Obtain Consent to Establish (CTE)
action_required: Apply for and obtain Consent to Establish under the Water Act before commencement of construction or installation of any outlet likely to discharge sewage/trade effluent.
forms_documents: CTE Application, Project Report, Layout Plan
frequency: Before commencement of construction or installation
penalty: Imprisonment 1 year 6 months to 6 years and fine under Section 44.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
brief_description: Prohibition on Pollution of Water
action_required: Ensure no poisonous, noxious or polluting matter is discharged into any stream, well or sewer without treatment, in line with the Water Act's pollution-prohibition provisions.
penalty: Imprisonment not less than 1 year 6 months, extendable to 6 years, with fine.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
brief_description: Responsibility of Occupier
action_required: As occupier of hazardous/other waste generating premises, take responsibility for environmentally sound handling, storage and disposal of such waste as prescribed.
penalty: Action under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 including penalties under Section 15.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
brief_description: Authorization
action_required: Apply for and obtain authorisation from the State Pollution Control Board before generating, storing, treating, transporting or disposing of hazardous/other waste.
penalty: Before commencement of activity; renewal before expiry

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
brief_description: Annual Return
action_required: Prepare and file the Annual Return on hazardous/other waste generation and disposal with the State Pollution Control Board by the prescribed date each year.
penalty: On or before 30th June following the financial year-Action under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for non-submission.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Construction & Demolition Waste
action_required: Segregate, store and process construction & demolition waste at source on an ongoing basis in compliance with the Solid Waste Management Rules.
penalty: Penalty under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
brief_description: Disposal to Landfill
action_required: Ensure only waste that cannot be processed/recycled is sent to landfill, and route it through authorised disposal facilities as per Rule 15(zi).
penalty: Statutory action under the Environment (Protection) Act

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Every waste generator shall be responsible for collection, segregation of concrete, soil and others and storage of construction and demolition waste generated, as directed or notified by the concerned local authority.
action_required: As waste generator, collect, segregate (concrete, soil, etc.) and store C&D waste as directed/notified by the local authority.
forms_documents: Form A Online Application & Fee Challan
penalty: Action under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, including directions, fines and prosecution.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: The generator shall ensure that other waste (such as solid waste) does not get mixed with construction and demolition waste and is stored and disposed separately.
action_required: Keep other solid waste streams separate from construction & demolition waste and arrange separate storage and disposal for each.
penalty: Environmental enforcement action and local authority penalties.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generators generating more than 20 tonnes in one day or 300 tonnes per project in a month shall segregate waste into separate streams including concrete, soil, steel, wood and plastics, bricks and mortar.
action_required: Where C&D waste generation exceeds 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/project/month, segregate waste into concrete, soil, steel, wood, plastics, bricks and mortar streams.
penalty: Refusal of project permissions and environmental action.
applicability: Applicable only where C&D waste generation exceeds 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/project/month

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generators generating more than 20 tonnes per day or 300 tonnes per month shall submit waste management plan and obtain approvals before construction, demolition or remodelling work.
action_required: For generation above the 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/month threshold, prepare and submit a Waste Management Plan and obtain approval before starting construction/demolition/remodelling.
penalty: Project approval may be withheld; environmental proceedings may be initiated.
applicability: Applicable only where C&D waste generation exceeds 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/project/month

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generators shall obtain appropriate approvals from the local authority before starting construction, demolition or remodelling work.
action_required: Obtain the requisite approvals from the local authority before commencing construction, demolition or remodelling work generating C&D waste.
penalty: Stop-work directions and penalties under applicable municipal laws.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generators shall keep the concerned authorities informed regarding relevant activities from planning stage to implementation stage.
action_required: Keep the local authority informed of C&D waste-related activities from the planning stage through implementation.
penalty: Non-compliance may lead to revocation of approvals and enforcement action.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Every waste generator shall keep construction and demolition waste within the premises.
action_required: Store construction and demolition waste within project premises pending collection/disposal, as required.
forms_documents: Form G Application for Agent Registration
penalty: Fines and removal costs imposed by local authority.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generator may get the waste deposited at collection centres established by local authorities.
action_required: Where available, deposit C&D waste at collection centres established by the local authority.
forms_documents: Form J Application for Agent Renewal
penalty: Recovery of transportation/removal costs.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generator may hand over construction and demolition waste to authorized processing facilities.
action_required: Hand over C&D waste to authorised processing facilities for recycling/disposal.
penalty: Unauthorized disposal may attract environmental penalties.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generator shall ensure that there is no littering or deposition of construction and demolition waste so as to prevent obstruction to traffic, public or drains.
action_required: Ensure C&D waste is not littered or deposited so as to obstruct traffic, public areas or drains, and arrange proper containment at site.
penalty: Clean-up costs, municipal fines and environmental action.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Every waste generator shall pay relevant charges for disposal of construction and demolition waste.
action_required: Pay the disposal charges for C&D waste as notified by the local authority.
forms_documents: Form 5 Annual Audit Report uploaded on Portal
penalty: Recovery proceedings by authority.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generators generating more than 20 tonnes per day or 300 tonnes per month shall pay for processing and disposal of waste generated in addition to storage, collection and transportation charges.
action_required: For generators above the 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/month threshold, additionally pay for processing and disposal over and above storage, collection and transportation charges.
penalty: Recovery of dues and enforcement action.
applicability: Applicable only where C&D waste generation exceeds 20 tonnes/day or 300 tonnes/project/month

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016
brief_description: Waste generator shall comply with directions issued by the local authority relating to collection, segregation, storage, transportation and disposal of construction and demolition waste.
action_required: Comply with all directions issued by the local authority on collection, segregation, storage, transportation and disposal of C&D waste.
forms_documents: Form N Compensation Claim / Reply Statement
penalty: Action under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

brief_description: Identify personal data collected from customers, employees, vendors, visitors, brokers and other individuals and map processing activities.
action_required: Conduct a one-time data mapping exercise to identify all personal data collected from customers, employees, vendors, visitors and brokers, and keep the data inventory updated on a continuous basis.
penalty: Penalty under Section 33 / Schedule, as applicable.

brief_description: Process personal data only for a lawful purpose based on consent or legitimate uses permitted by the Act.
action_required: Process personal data only on the basis of valid consent or a permitted legitimate use, and periodically audit processing activities against this requirement.
penalty: Penalty up to ₹50 crore for other breaches, subject to Schedule.

brief_description:
Give clear notice specifying personal data collected and purpose of processing.
Ensure notice is presented independently, in clear and plain language, and provides the required information enabling informed consent.

Provide information regarding how the Data Principal can exercise rights under the Act and how a complaint can be made to the Board.
action_required: Issue an independent, clear-language notice at the point of data collection specifying the personal data collected, purpose of processing, and how to exercise rights or complain to the Board.
penalty: Penalty under Section 33 / Schedule.

brief_description:
Obtain consent that is free, specific, informed and unambiguous, with clear affirmative action, for processing personal data for the specified purpose.

Provide a mechanism to withdraw consent that is as easy as giving consent.

Maintain evidence demonstrating that valid consent was obtained in accordance with the Act.
action_required: Implement a consent mechanism that captures free, specific, informed and unambiguous affirmative consent, provide an equally easy withdrawal option, and retain consent records as evidence.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule, where applicable.

brief_description:
Document and verify cases where processing is undertaken under legitimate-use grounds rather than consent.

Process personal data without obtaining consent only where such processing falls within the specified ‘certain legitimate uses’ under Section 7 of the DPDP Act, 2023. Ensure that the processing is undertaken only for the permitted purpose, limited to the personal data necessary for that purpose, and supported by appropriate records demonstrating the applicable legitimate-use basis.”
action_required: Where processing without consent, document and verify that it falls strictly within a Section 7 legitimate-use ground, limit it to necessary data, and retain supporting records.
penalty: Penalty under Section 33 / Schedule.

brief_description: Ensure personal data is accurate and complete where necessary for decisions affecting the Data Principal or disclosure to another Data Fiduciary.
action_required: Implement data-quality checks to ensure personal data used for decisions affecting a Data Principal, or shared with another Data Fiduciary, is accurate and complete.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description:
Notify the Data Protection Board and affected Data Principals in the event of a personal data breach, in the prescribed manner.

Notify the Data Protection Board of India without delay. (Nature, Extent, Date and Time, Circumstances, Likely impact, Measures taken)
A detailed update must be furnished within 72 hours, unless the Board permits a longer period.
action_required: On any personal data breach, notify the Data Protection Board of India without delay and affected Data Principals as prescribed, furnishing a detailed update within 72 hours.
penalty: Up to ₹200 crore

brief_description: Erase personal data when its purpose is no longer served, subject to legal retention requirements.
action_required: Set up and follow a data retention/erasure schedule to erase personal data once its purpose is served, subject to legal retention requirements.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description: Obtain verifiable consent of the parent/lawful guardian before processing personal data of a child.
action_required: Before processing any child's personal data, obtain verifiable parental/guardian consent and apply the additional restrictions prescribed for children's data.
penalty: Up to ₹200 crore
applicability: Applicable only where the company processes personal data of children (below 18 years)

brief_description: Provide Data Principal information regarding personal data being processed and prescribed details.
action_required: On request, provide Data Principals with a summary of their personal data being processed and the other prescribed details.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description:
Provide mechanism for correction of inaccurate data and erasure where legally required.

Complete personal data where the Data Principal identifies that information is incomplete.

Update outdated personal data based on a valid request.

Erase personal data upon a valid erasure request unless retention is necessary for the specified purpose or required by law.
action_required: Implement a mechanism to correct, complete, update or erase personal data on a valid Data Principal request, subject to permitted retention exceptions.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description:
Establish an accessible grievance redressal mechanism.

Investigate and respond to grievances within the period prescribed under the Rules or applicable law.

Ensure the Data Principal has an opportunity to use the company's grievance mechanism before approaching the Board.

Respond to the grievance within the period prescribed under applicable law; where no period is prescribed, follow the period specified under the Rules.
action_required: Set up an accessible grievance redressal mechanism, respond within the prescribed timeline, and ensure Data Principals can use it before approaching the Board.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description: Provide mechanism for Data Principal to nominate another individual to exercise rights in specified circumstances.
action_required: Provide a mechanism for Data Principals to nominate another individual to exercise their rights in the event of death or incapacity.
penalty: Penalty under Schedule.

brief_description: Respond to inquiries, complaints and directions of the Data Protection Board.
action_required: Respond promptly and fully to inquiries, complaints and directions issued by the Data Protection Board.
penalty: Penalty / directions as applicable.

brief_description:
File appeal against Board orders where required.

If aggrieved by an order/direction of the Data Protection Board, assess whether an appeal should be filed before the Appellate Tribunal.

If the appeal is filed after 60 days, provide sufficient cause for delay and seek condonation from the Appellate Tribunal.
action_required: On receipt of an adverse Board order, evaluate the merits and file an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal within 60 days, seeking condonation with sufficient cause if delayed.
penalty: Order may become final if appeal is not filed in time.

brief_description:
Ensure electronic records used by the company are maintained in a legally reliable manner.

Ensure documents/information required to be in writing can be generated, stored or made available electronically.
action_required: Ensure electronic records and documents required to be in writing are generated, stored and retrieved in a manner that meets IT Act legal-reliability requirements.
penalty: Legal validity of records may be affected if statutory requirements are not met.

brief_description: Use valid electronic/digital signatures for documents requiring electronic authentication.
action_required: Use valid electronic/digital signatures issued by a licensed certifying authority for documents requiring electronic authentication.
penalty: Invalid authentication and related legal consequences.

brief_description: Safeguard electronic signature certificates and private keys; prevent unauthorised use.
action_required: Implement controls to safeguard electronic signature certificates and private keys, and prevent their unauthorised use.
penalty: Liability under applicable provisions of the Act. (India Code)

brief_description: Prevent unauthorised access, downloading, copying, introducing malware, disruption or damage to computer resources.
action_required: Deploy technical safeguards (access controls, anti-malware, monitoring) to prevent unauthorised access, downloading, copying or damage to computer resources.
penalty: Compensation to affected person for damage caused. (India Code)

brief_description: Prevent unauthorised disclosure of electronic records/information obtained under statutory powers.
action_required: Restrict and log access to electronic records/information obtained under statutory powers to prevent unauthorised disclosure.
penalty: Penalty up to ₹5 lakh. (India Code)

brief_description: Ensure employees, consultants, vendors and service providers do not disclose personal information obtained under lawful contracts without consent or contrary to contract.
action_required: Bind employees, consultants, vendors and service providers under confidentiality/contractual clauses restricting disclosure of personal information obtained under lawful contracts.
penalty: Penalty up to ₹25 lakh. (India Code)

brief_description:
Identify sensitive personal data/information collected or processed by the company.

Passwords, Financial information such as bank account, credit/debit card or other payment instrument details,Physical, physiological and mental health condition,Sexual orientation,Medical records and history,Biometric information
action_required: Carry out a one-time identification exercise (with periodic review) to map all sensitive personal data or information (passwords, financial data, health data, biometrics, etc.) held by the company.
penalty: Non-compliance may attract consequences under Section 43A.
applicability: Applicable only where the company collects/processes SPDI

brief_description: Treat passwords, financial information, physical/mental health condition, sexual orientation, medical records, biometric information and similar prescribed information as SPDI.
action_required: Classify and handle passwords, financial information, health/medical data, sexual orientation, and biometric information as SPDI with enhanced safeguards on an ongoing basis.
penalty: Section 43A consequences.
applicability: Applicable only where the company collects/processes SPDI

brief_description:
Publish a clear and easily accessible privacy policy explaining the company's practices and policies for handling personal information/SPDI.

Specify the types of personal information and SPDI collected by the company.

State the purposes for which personal information/SPDI is collected and used.

Explain the circumstances and manner in which personal information/SPDI may be disclosed, in accordance with Rule 6.

Describe the reasonable security practices and procedures implemented under Rule 8.
action_required: Publish and keep updated a clear privacy policy covering the personal information/SPDI collected, purposes, disclosure practices and security measures under Rule 8.
penalty: Section 43A consequences.
applicability: Applicable only where the company collects/processes personal information/SPDI

brief_description: Obtain consent before collecting SPDI, subject to permitted circumstances.
action_required: Obtain consent before collecting SPDI from an individual, except in the circumstances permitted under the Rules.
penalty: Section 43A consequences.
applicability: Applicable only where the company collects SPDI

brief_description: Do not disclose SPDI to third parties without prior permission, except where permitted by law/contract or required by lawful authority.
action_required: Do not disclose SPDI to third parties without the provider's prior permission, except where permitted by law/contract or required by a lawful authority.
penalty: Section 43A consequences.
applicability: Applicable only where the company discloses SPDI to third parties

brief_description: Provide SPDI to Government agencies when disclosure is legally required for specified purposes.
action_required: Provide SPDI to Government agencies on receipt of a valid legal request for the specified statutory purposes.
penalty: Legal consequences for failure to comply.
applicability: Applicable only where a Government agency legally requests SPDI

brief_description: Transfer SPDI to another body corporate/person only where necessary for lawful purposes and subject to applicable consent/contractual and security requirements.
action_required: Before transferring SPDI to another body corporate or person, verify the necessity, obtain consent where required, and ensure equivalent security safeguards under contract.
penalty: Section 43A consequences.
applicability: Applicable only where SPDI is transferred to another body corporate/person

brief_description: Conduct periodic review/audit of security controls and practices.
action_required: Conduct a periodic review/audit of information security controls and practices as required under Rule 8(3).
penalty: Section 43A consequences.

brief_description:
Report specified cyber-security incidents to CERT-In.

Report available information concerning the incident. Complete information need not be available at the initial 6-hour reporting stage.
action_required: On occurrence of a reportable cyber-security incident, report available information to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing/being notified, updating as more facts emerge.
due_date: Within 6 hours of noticing the incident or being brought to notice
penalty: Under Section 70B(7): imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹1 lakh, or both. (CERT-In)

brief_description: Identify incidents falling within CERT-In's specified categories, including unauthorised access, data breach, phishing, ransomware, DDoS, malware, website compromise and attacks on critical systems.
action_required: Maintain continuous monitoring capability to identify CERT-In notifiable incidents (unauthorised access, data breach, phishing, ransomware, DDoS, malware, website compromise, attacks on critical systems).
penalty: Same Section 70B(7) consequence for failure to comply with directions. (CERT-In)

brief_description: Designate a Point of Contact for communication with CERT-In.
action_required: Designate a Point of Contact for CERT-In communications and keep the nomination updated whenever the person changes.
due_date: Before operational compliance / whenever details change
penalty: Section 70B(7) for failure to comply with direction. (CERT-In)

brief_description:
Enable logs for all ICT systems and maintain them securely.

Maintain ICT system logs securely for a rolling period of at least 180 days.

Submit relevant logs to CERT-In along with reporting of a cyber incident.

Provide logs when CERT-In specifically orders/directs the company to do so.
action_required: Enable logging across all ICT systems, retain logs securely for a rolling 180 days, and submit them to CERT-In when reporting an incident or on specific direction.
penalty: Section 70B(7). (CERT-In)

regulation: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
brief_description:
Register establishment under EPF if applicable, criteria It applies to covered factories and other establishments employing 20 or more persons, subject to Section 16 exemptions and the notified categories, 
Register on: EPFO Portal (Online)
action_required: Once headcount reaches 20 or more (subject to Section 16 exemptions), register the establishment under EPF on the EPFO portal within the prescribed time.
penalty: Penalty for non-registration
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment employs 20 or more persons (subject to Section 16 exemptions)

regulation: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
brief_description:
Deposit the applicable employer contribution to the EPF Fund.
Deduct the employee's applicable EPF contribution from wages and deposit it with EPFO.
The statutory rate is generally 12% for establishments/classes covered by the notified 12% rate; the Act's base provision refers to 10%, with the notified modification substituting 12%. Contributions are calculated on basic wages + dearness allowance + retaining allowance, if any
action_required: Deduct the employee's EPF contribution from wages, add the employer's matching contribution (12% of basic + DA + retaining allowance, as notified), and deposit both with EPFO by the monthly due date.
penalty: Interest (Sec. 7Q) & Damages (Sec. 14B)
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under EPF

regulation: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
brief_description:
Submit the prescribed consolidated return of employees required/entitled to become EPF members, including applicable wage particulars.
1.Submit the prescribed return for employees becoming EPF members for the first time during the preceding month.
2.Report employees who left service during the preceding month in the prescribed manner.
3.Where applicable, submit a NIL return if there are no new qualifying members or employees leaving service.
action_required: File the monthly consolidated EPF return (new joiners, leavers, and NIL return where applicable) with prescribed wage particulars by the due date.
penalty: Penalty for non-enrolment
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under EPF

regulation: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
brief_description: Submit a statement to the Principal Employer showing the EPF contribution recoveries relating to employees employed by/through the contractor. Statement must be submitted within 7 days from the close of every month.
action_required: As/through contractor, submit the statement of EPF contribution recoveries for contract employees to the Principal Employer within 7 days of the close of each month.
penalty: Compliance observations
applicability: Applicable only where contract labour is engaged and EPF applies to those employees

regulation: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
brief_description:
Furnish information/documents requested by an EPFO Inspector.
Allow the Inspector to enter and inspect the establishment/premises at a reasonable time.
Produce accounts, books, registers and other documents relating to employment and payment of wages.
action_required: On request from an EPFO Inspector, furnish the requisite information/documents, permit inspection of premises, and produce wage and employment registers.
penalty: Fine/Prosecution
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is registered/covered under EPF

brief_description:
Applicable where 10 or more persons are employed, subject to applicable notifications.
ESI coverage generally applies to employees whose monthly wages do not exceed ₹21,000. For persons with disability, the ceiling is ₹25,000.
action_required: Once 10 or more persons are employed, assess ESI applicability for employees drawing wages up to ₹21,000/month (₹25,000 for persons with disability) and enrol them on joining.
penalty: Penalty for non-registration
applicability: Applicable only where 10 or more persons are employed, subject to wage-ceiling notifications

brief_description:
Deposit employer's ESI contribution at 3.25% of wages.
Deduct employee's ESI contribution at 0.75% of wages, where applicable.
action_required: Deduct the employee's ESI contribution (0.75% of wages) and deposit the employer's contribution (3.25% of wages) with ESIC every month by the due date.
penalty: Delayed payment attracts simple interest at 12% p.a. or the higher rate permitted under the regulations, subject to the statutory limit.
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under ESI

brief_description:
Submit prescribed returns to ESIC containing particulars of employees and the establishment in the prescribed form/manner.
Maintain Form 6/Register of Employees containing prescribed particulars of every employee, including name, insurance number, date of birth, date of appointment, nature of employment, wages, contribution details and date/reason for leaving service, and keep the register available for ESIC inspection
action_required: File the prescribed periodic ESI returns and maintain Form 6/Register of Employees with all prescribed particulars, available for ESIC inspection.
penalty: Fine
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under ESI

brief_description: Ensure timely and accurate payment of ESI contributions to prevent loss or reduction of employee benefits; monitor and reconcile contributions regularly and promptly rectify any default, as ESIC may recover from the principal employer the greater of the benefit difference or twice the unpaid contribution
action_required: Reconcile ESI contribution deposits regularly and rectify any shortfall/default promptly to avoid recovery action by ESIC.
penalty: Penalty
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under ESI

brief_description:
Furnish information/documents requested by the SSO for ESI verification.
Permit the SSO to enter the office, factory or establishment at a reasonable time.
Produce books, accounts, registers and other documents relating to employment and payment of wages.
action_required: On request from the Social Security Officer, furnish requested information/documents, permit entry/inspection, and produce wage and employment records.
penalty: Penalty
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment is covered under ESI

brief_description:
No employer shall pay to any employee wages less than
the minimum rate of wages notified by the appropriate Government.
action_required: Pay every employee at least the minimum rate of wages notified by the appropriate Government; audit payroll periodically for compliance.
penalty: Fine

brief_description: sets the legal time limits for Employers to disburse wages to employees based on their wage period cycle. It ensures timely payouts across all employment types, regardless of a wage ceiling.
action_required: Disburse wages to employees within the statutory time limit applicable to their wage period, for every category of employment.
penalty: Penalty

brief_description:
Pay statutory bonus to every eligible employee drawing wages up to the wage ceiling notified by the Appropriate Government, provided the employee has worked for at least 30 days in the accounting year.
Pay a minimum annual bonus of 8⅓% of the wages earned or ₹100, whichever is higher, even if there is no allocable surplus
action_required: Compute and pay statutory bonus to every eligible employee (worked 30+ days in the accounting year) at a minimum of 8-1/3% of wages or Rs.100, whichever is higher, even absent allocable surplus.
penalty: Penalty

brief_description: Display at a prominent place in the establishment an abstract of the Code, category-wise wage rates, wage period, date/time of wage payment, and the name and address of the jurisdictional Inspector-cum-Facilitator.
action_required: Display, at a prominent place, an abstract of the Code, category-wise wage rates, wage period, payment date/time and the jurisdictional Inspector-cum-Facilitator's details.
penalty: Fine

brief_description:
Generally applies to establishments covered by the Code, including establishments with 10 or more workers, subject to specific provisions/exclusions.
Employer must apply electronically to the registering officer appointed by the appropriate Government.
Application within 60 days from the date the Code becomes applicable to the establishment.
action_required: Once covered (10+ workers), apply electronically to the registering officer for OSH Code registration within 60 days of the Code becoming applicable.
penalty: Fine of ₹2 lakh to ₹3 lakh for a first offence, with higher consequences for subsequent/continuing contraventions as prescribed under the penalty framework
applicability: Applicable only where the establishment employs 10 or more workers (subject to exclusions)

brief_description: Ensure that machinery, equipment and other articles designed, manufactured, imported or supplied for use in the establishment are safe when properly used, are appropriately tested/examined, and are accompanied by adequate information regarding intended use and necessary safety precautions.
action_required: Ensure machinery, equipment and articles used are safety-tested, accompanied by usage/safety information, and reviewed annually for continued compliance.
penalty: Fine

brief_description:
Provide and maintain all prescribed welfare facilities, including washing and bathing facilities, locker rooms, seating arrangements, canteen, first-aid, rest/shelter rooms, ambulance room, welfare officer and crèche facilities, wherever the prescribed applicability thresholds are met.
Establishments employing more than 50 workers must provide crèche facilities as prescribed.
action_required: Provide and maintain the prescribed welfare facilities (washing/bathing, locker rooms, seating, canteen, first-aid, rest rooms, ambulance room, welfare officer, and crèche for 50+ workers) on an ongoing basis.
penalty: Penalty
applicability: Crèche facility requirement applicable only where more than 50 workers are employed

brief_description:
Arrange medical examination of workers in the prescribed manner and at prescribed intervals.
Ensure workers exposed to specified hazardous processes, dangerous operations or occupational risks undergo required medical examinations.
Conduct medical examinations where prescribed before employment and periodically thereafter.
action_required: Arrange pre-employment and periodic medical examinations for workers, especially those exposed to hazardous processes, per the prescribed intervals.
penalty: Penalty

brief_description:
Report accidents causing death, bodily injury resulting in inability to work for 48 hours or more, and other prescribed accidents.
Report prescribed dangerous occurrences whether or not they cause injury or disability.
action_required: Report to the authority every fatal accident, injury causing 48+ hours' incapacity, and other prescribed accidents/dangerous occurrences as they occur.
penalty: Fine/Prosecution

brief_description: Maintain complete and up-to-date statutory registers and records covering worker particulars, working hours, weekly rest, wages, leave, overtime, attendance, dangerous occurrences and adolescent employment; issue wage slips and file prescribed returns with the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within the applicable timelines
action_required: Maintain up-to-date statutory registers (worker particulars, hours, wages, leave, overtime, attendance), issue wage slips, and file returns with the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within timelines.
penalty: Fine

brief_description:
Pay statutory compensation where an employee suffers an employment-related injury covered under the Act.
Ensure accidents occurring arising out of and in the course of employment are assessed for compensation liability.
action_required: Assess every employment-related injury for compensation liability and pay statutory compensation where the Act applies.
penalty: Interest & Penalty

brief_description: Compensation payable under Section 4 must be paid as soon as it falls due
action_required:
Assess liability immediately
Investigate the accident/injury and determine whether compensation is payable under the Act.

Calculate compensation
Compute the compensation amount as per Section 4 based on wages, age, and nature of injury/death.

Pay compensation without delay
Ensure compensation is paid as soon as it falls due and preferably within one month to avoid statutory consequences.

Make provisional payment if liability is disputed
Where the employer does not accept the full claim, pay the admitted amount provisionally by depositing it with the Commissioner or paying the employee.

Maintain documentation
Keep records of accident reports, compensation calculations, payment proofs, insurance correspondence, and acknowledgements from employees/dependents.

Coordinate with insurer
If covered under a Workmen's/Employees' Compensation Insurance Policy, notify the insurer immediately and process the claim as per policy requirements.

Avoid delayed payment
Delays beyond one month may attract:
Interest at 12% p.a. or applicable notified rate; and
Penalty up to 50% of the compensation amount if the delay is unjustified
penalty: Interest at 12% p.a. (or applicable higher notified rate within the statutory limit) plus, where unjustified delay is established, a penalty of up to 50% of the compensation amount.

compliance_type: Project Level (To be mapped against each live and new project)
regulation: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016
brief_description: Promoter shall update project information as prescribed by regulations.
action_required:
Create and maintain the project webpage on the RERA Authority portal and ensure it remains active and accessible throughout the project lifecycle.
Upload and regularly update prescribed project information, including:
Number and types of apartments/plots booked.
Number of garages booked.
Approvals obtained and approvals pending after commencement certificate.
Current project status, including construction progress and stage-wise completion status.
Stage-wise construction photographs.
Registration details, approved plans, layouts, and other project documents.
Any additional information, documents, and disclosures prescribed by the applicable State RERA Authority.
For projects registered with MahaRERA, submit Quarterly Progress Reports (QPRs) covering:
Construction progress and completion status.
Number of units booked versus available units.
Status of approvals and permissions.
Financial disclosures, including project fund utilization and withdrawals.
Architect's, Engineer's, and Chartered Accountant's certifications, where applicable.

regulation: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
brief_description:
Permission granted by the Planning Authority may be subject to such general or special conditions as the Planning Authority may impose.
Examples of General or Special Conditions
Compliance with approved building plans and layout.
Obtaining all statutory approvals/NOCs before commencement or occupancy.
Provision of parking, access roads, and internal circulation facilities.
Fire safety, structural stability, and building safety requirements.
Environmental protection measures, including waste management and pollution control.
Storm-water drainage, water supply, and sewage disposal arrangements.
Provision and maintenance of open spaces, amenities, and common facilities.
Restrictions on change of land use, building height, FSI/FAR, or density.
Traffic management and infrastructure improvement requirements.
Compliance with conditions imposed by other regulatory authorities.
action_required:
Review all conditions attached to the planning permission.
Maintain a register/tracker of applicable conditions.
Implement each condition within the prescribed timeline.
Obtain required NOCs, approvals, and certifications.
Maintain documentary evidence of compliance.
Ensure continued compliance throughout construction and occupancy stages.
Seek approval from the Planning Authority before deviating from approved conditions
penalty: Permission may be revoked and enforcement proceedings may be initiated.

regulation: Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966
brief_description: Any person who commences, undertakes or carries out development without permission or contrary to permission granted shall be guilty of unauthorized development.

penalty: Imprisonment which may extend to 3 years and/or fine which may extend to ₹5,000; continuing offence may attract additional daily fine as prescribed.

Obtain all development permissions from the relevant Special Planning Authority.
Ensure construction and land development comply with SPA-approved plans and conditions.
Obtain required commencement, layout, and occupancy approvals from the SPA.
Comply with development control regulations applicable to the notified area.
Maintain records of permissions, approvals, NOCs, and correspondence with the Special Planning Authority.
penalty: Development may be declared unauthorized and subjected to enforcement action.

regulation: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
brief_description: The Act shall apply when the Government acquires land for public purpose and for rehabilitation and resettlement connected therewith.
action_required:
The Act applies when the Appropriate Government acquires land for:

Government use, hold and control, including for Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs).
Public Purpose Projects, including:

Strategic and defence purposes.
Infrastructure projects.
Industrial corridors and manufacturing zones.
Water supply, sanitation, and conservation projects.
Government educational and research institutions.
Housing projects.
Planned urban and rural development.
Rehabilitation of project-affected families.

Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Projects

Where ownership of the land continues to vest with the Government.
Requires prior consent of at least 70% of affected families.

Private Company Projects for Public Purpose

Acquisition is permitted only for a recognized public purpose.
Requires prior consent of at least 80% of affected families.

Rehabilitation and Resettlement

Whenever acquisition displaces affected families and triggers R&R obligations under the Act.
Action Required for Compliance
Confirm that the acquisition falls within a permitted public purpose.
Conduct a Social Impact Assessment (SIA) where required.
Obtain prescribed consent from affected families for PPP/private projects.
Pay compensation as determined under the Act.
Implement Rehabilitation & Resettlement (R&R) measures.
Maintain all acquisition notifications, consent records, compensation awards, and R&R documentation
forms_documents: Valid Lift Working License framed in Lift Car
penalty: Acquisition process may be invalid if Act requirements are not followed.
applicability: Conditional - applicable only if the Government initiates compulsory acquisition of the company's project land for a public purpose
